cases.situation: My coworker Dave takes speakerphone calls at his desk in our open office almost every morning. I sit right next to him and can't focus. We get along fine.
cases.reply: Hey Dave, small thing: the speakerphone calls in the mornings carry right over to my desk and I lose my train of thought when I'm writing. Could you take them on headphones, or grab one of the phone booths? Happy to return the favour if I'm ever the noisy one.
cases.note: One behaviour, the effect in first person, and a concrete alternative with two easy options.

cases.situation: 我老公每次跟我妈吃饭都一直刷手机，我妈嘴上不说但我看得出她不开心。想跟他提一下但不想吵架。
cases.reply: 老公，跟你说个小事，不是要吵架哈。每次跟我妈吃饭的时候你基本都在看手机，我妈其实挺在意的，我坐旁边也有点难受。以后跟她吃饭那一个多小时，手机能不能先放兜里？有急事的话跟她说一声再看就行，我也一样。
cases.note: 只说一个具体行为和对自己的影响，请求具体到那一个多小时，并把自己也放进同一个规则里。

cases.situation: I already asked my roommate Sam a month ago to stop leaving his bike in the hallway, he did for a week and now it's back. I trip on it every morning.
cases.reply: Hey Sam, I mentioned the bike in the hallway a few weeks ago and it's crept back. I'm not trying to nag, I've actually tripped on it twice this week. Could we put up a wall hook in your room or the storage cupboard this weekend? I'll pick one up and help you mount it.
cases.note: Second ask: name that it slipped, restate the effect, and offer a fix that makes the new habit easier.

cases.situation: 楼上邻居最近每天晚上11点以后还在拖椅子、走路很响，我12点前要睡，早上6点起。跟他们不认识，只知道是1802，想在他家门上贴张纸条。
cases.reply: 1802的邻居您好，我是楼下1702的小林。最近晚上11点以后，楼上拖椅子和走路的声音在我家听得挺清楚，我早上6点要起床，有时会被吵醒。能不能11点以后稍微轻一点？我多买了一包椅子脚垫，如果您用得上，我放在您门口。谢谢您！
cases.note: 不认识的邻居就用纸条，默认对方不知道；只说一个具体行为和时间段，再附一个很容易做到的办法。

cases.situation: My mum keeps posting photos of our 4-month-old, Leo, on her public Facebook. She's so proud and I don't want to hurt her, but we'd rather he wasn't online. Texting her.
cases.reply: Hi Mum, small thing, and definitely not a telling-off: the photos of Leo on your Facebook, we'd rather keep him off public posts for now. We just feel better keeping his pictures within the family. Could you share them in the family WhatsApp instead? I'll keep sending you plenty, I promise.
cases.note: With a parent, name the one behaviour, give them a better place for the pride, and keep the reason about your comfort, not their judgement.

cases.situation: A senior director, Paul, calls me 'kiddo' in meetings, including in front of clients. I'm 31 and the project lead. He's friendly and probably doesn't realise. Want to message him privately on Teams.
cases.reply: Hi Paul, a small thing I wanted to raise privately. You've called me 'kiddo' a few times in client meetings, most recently with the Hollis team last Thursday. I know it's meant warmly, but in front of clients it undercuts me as the lead on their project. Would you mind just using Anna? Thanks, I appreciate it.
cases.note: Upward and across a power gap: private, one dated example, the effect on the work rather than on feelings, and an ask that is easy to say yes to.

cases.situation: I asked my girlfriend Mei to put her phone on silent after we're in bed because the buzzing keeps waking me. She shot back: 'well, you snore and I never complain.'
cases.reply: Fair, the snoring is real, and I'll book a GP appointment about it this week. I'm not having a go at you; it's just the buzzing that keeps waking me. Could we try silent after we're in bed from tonight?
cases.note: When they say 'you do it too', concede what's true and go back to the one ask instead of trading grievances.

cases.situation: My friend Leila turns up 20 to 40 minutes late to basically every Sunday brunch we do. I've never said anything and I end up holding a table on my own. Next one is this Sunday, October 4, at 11.
cases.reply: Hey Leila, small thing before Sunday, not a big deal: at most of our brunches you've got there 20 to 40 minutes after we said, and I end up alone at the table fending off the waiter. Could you text me when you're actually leaving home? Then I'll set off to match and we'll arrive together. Still on for 11 at Maple?
cases.note: One behaviour, the effect on you, and a shared system that doesn't require her to become punctual overnight.

cases.situation: 我和室友小雅合租两居室，房租水电平摊。她男朋友阿凯最近基本每周住五天，早上洗手间要排队，上个月电费也多了快一百。我跟她关系挺好，不想闹僵。
cases.reply: 小雅，跟你商量个事哈，不是要闹什么。最近阿凯差不多每周住五天，早上洗手间经常要排队，上个月电费也多了快一百块。我们能不能定个规矩，一周留宿最多两晚？要是他想常来，水电费分成三份也可以，你看哪种更顺？我这边朋友来住也按同样的规矩来。
cases.note: 只说一件事和对自己的影响，把请求说成两个人共同的规矩，并给对方一个选项。

cases.situation: My younger brother Kyle borrows my car most weekends, which I'm fine with. But it almost always comes back with the fuel light on, and twice this month I've been late for work because I had to stop for petrol first thing Monday. He's borrowing it again this Saturday.
cases.reply: Hey, small car thing before Saturday. It's come back on the fuel light a few times lately, and twice this month that's made me late for work on Monday morning. Could we go with a simple rule: it comes back with at least a quarter tank? Happy to keep lending it, that's the only ask.
cases.note: One behaviour, the concrete effect on you, and a rule that's easy to check, with the lending itself not in question.

cases.situation: My teammate Ryan keeps cutting me off in our Monday planning meetings, usually just as I get to my recommendation. It's happened three weeks running. We're peers and get along fine. Want to DM him on Slack before next Monday.
cases.reply: Hey Ryan, small thing before Monday. In the last few planning meetings you've come in just as I was getting to my recommendation, so the team ends up hearing half the idea. I doubt it's noticeable from your side. Could you let me finish the point, then jump in? Happy to do the same for you, and tell me if I'm going on too long.
cases.note: One observable behaviour, a private channel, and an ask he can act on in the moment; offering the same back keeps it between peers.
